title: Gaiada - Host & Infrastructure
description: MON-09l. The box itself: CPU, memory, disk, load, containers and datastore reachability. This existed nowhere before -- every other Gaiada dashboard is application-level, and checking all four for node_*/container_*/pg_*/redis_* returned zero matches, which is how two completely blind datastore exporters went unnoticed for weeks.

panels.title: CPU busy %
panels.description: Whole-host busy percentage. This box has no per-core panel on purpose: at this size the aggregate is the decision, and 8 idle cores hide one saturated one either way.

panels.title: Memory used %
panels.description: Uses MemAvailable, not MemFree. MemFree excludes reclaimable page cache and makes a healthy Linux box look nearly full.

panels.title: Disk used % (/)
panels.description: Same expression as the DiskSpaceLow alert (fires below 15% free). Kept identical deliberately: a dashboard that stays green while the pager fires teaches people to distrust the dashboard.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Compare against core count, not against 1.0.

panels.title: Disk free, with 24h projection
panels.description: The projection is the actionable series: this box carries ~19 GB of release images for two tags and only reclaims on the next release, so free space steps down and drifts rather than sitting flat. `docker system df` reports near-zero reclaimable, so pruning is not a recovery lever here.

panels.title: Datastore reachability
panels.description: 1 = the exporter can reach the datastore; 0 = it cannot. This is NOT the same as the scrape target being up. Both of these read 0 for weeks while Prometheus showed both targets green, because the exporters pointed at container hostnames that are never started on this box. That is the whole reason this panel exists.

panels.title: Scrape targets down
panels.description: `or vector(0)` matters: with no targets down the inner query returns an EMPTY result, which draws as a gap and is indistinguishable from Prometheus being broken. The fallback makes healthy render as an explicit 0.

panels.title: Postgres backends by database
panels.description: Excludes template/postgres databases, which are always idle and only add legend noise.

options.content:
### Per-container metrics are not being collected

cAdvisor is running and its scrape target is **green**, but it emits only host cgroup series (`/`, `/init.scope`, `/system.slice/...`) with no `name` label, so there are no per-container CPU or memory metrics to graph.

Adding `/dev/kmsg` and `/dev/disk` cleared the `Failed to create existing container: /system.slice/docker-<hash>` errors, but container discovery still yields nothing on this cgroup-v2 host.

**Two working panels are deliberately not shown here rather than shown empty.** The queries are correct and will light up when the collector does:

```
topk(10, sum by (name) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{name!=""}[5m])) * 100)
topk(10, sum by (name) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{name!=""}))
```

Tracked as **MON-09n**. Note the pattern: this is the third collector found today that was *up* while collecting nothing (the two datastore exporters were the others). A green scrape target is not a passing check.
